one_star_reviews.text:
Extremely disappointing experience with Goundrys. After agreeing a sale and issuing a memorandum of sale, the property was re-advertised whilst I was simply waiting for the survey results to be returned, something I had clearly communicated from the outset before formally instructing solicitors and paying search funds.

The survey turnaround was only 7 working days, with results due back the same day I received notification the property had been placed back online. The handling of the situation felt unnecessarily pressurising and, in my opinion, highly unprofessional towards a serious buyer.

Small things throughout the process also added to the frustration, including poor communication, being repeatedly called by the wrong name in email communication, calls not being returned, and updates not being provided when promised. Individually these may seem minor, but collectively they reflected a lack of care and professionalism throughout the transaction.

As a first-time buyer, the process is already stressful enough without feeling rushed or undermined despite being transparent throughout. I have now walked away from the purchase having incurred significant costs with nothing to show for it and no home at the end of the process.

Overall, I found the experience very unprofessional and disappointing, and unfortunately it has left a very negative impression.

Based on my experience, I would strongly caution others before choosing to proceed with this estate agent.

Do better Goundrys.

I was recently offered the opportunity to view a property in Cornwall which unfortunately I could not attend due to living over three hundred miles away.

I was subsequently offered a video viewing which worked well under the circumstances. As I was keen to secure a property due to imminent relocation with my current employer I took the liberty of travelling down a couple of days before to carry out an external viewing  to ensure it was in a good location and as described.

On the day of the video viewing I sat and waited and waited and waited again....no call was received.  Based on this I contacted the office to ask what was going on before I was cut off mid conversation!

My message was passed on to the person carrying out the viewing who contacted me claiming that there was a misunderstanding on my part with regards to the viewing and that I would be sent a video once he had finished showing others around.

Having dealt with a number of estate agents in the county over the past few weeks I find it strange how all of them have managed to carry out a video viewing at an agreed time which not only allowed me to see the properties but also gave me the chance to speak directly with the agent and ask questions yet Goundrys couldn't manage this.

To me this demonstrates a complete lack of interest and effort which reflects badly on the company.

I did eventually receive the video via WhatsApp which had clearly been filmed at an earlier date as the to let sign which was outside the property was not present a couple of days before when I visited.

Despite replying to the message stating that I would like to proceed with the application nothing else was heard until a standard email of rejection was received several days later.

I don't particularly like leaving negative reviews for business's but the reality is first impressions count.

I had a disappointing experience with this emergency lockout locksmith service.

We explained from the outset that the door had a split spindle lock and was not deadlocked, meaning turning the internal handle would have opened the door. The locksmith initially attempted to gain entry using a plastic sheet and then advised that drilling the lock was the only viable option. Based on this professional advice, I agreed to proceed. This was an especially stressful situation as I was with my elderly parents and we had just returned from A&E, so we urgently needed to gain access to the property and relied on the locksmith’s professional advice.

However, after drilling the lock, the door was ultimately opened using a letterbox tool to operate the internal handle — a non-destructive method which had not been attempted beforehand.

My concern is that this method was not attempted before the lock was drilled and replaced. I was charged £418.80 in total, including replacement lock and installation costs. In my view, unnecessary and costly destructive work was carried out before all reasonable non-destructive methods had been attempted.

The company later stated that drilling was required to relieve pressure/load within the mechanism. However, this explanation regarding pressure/load within the mechanism was only provided retrospectively and could not have been definitively confirmed without first attempting to operate the internal handle directly. As no attempt was made to use the letterbox method beforehand, it was never demonstrated that drilling was genuinely necessary in order to gain entry.

I raised these concerns directly with the company, but they declined to offer any refund.

In my view, the overall charge was unreasonable and disproportionate given the circumstances.

gave a 4 week window after waiting over a year to be seen to complete questions, their replies to my answers took a period of time which were re asking the same questions and wasting my time.

they knew I had blood pressure medication and tried to prescribe me a medication that also affects it, my BP readings were consistent and I was continuously asked to send them again as they didn't like the results, then asked stupid questions wasting the 4 weeks.

Absolute worst way to handle ADHD patients! I got a letter sent to doctor blaming me for not engaging and taking no ownership of their failure to ask useful questions that would move us forward.

Absolute terrible company, if I knew what I knew now, I would have chosen a different company. I started my journey with psychiatry UK back in May 2024 via the right to choose pathway for an ADHD assessment.

I waited one year for my appointment and diagnosis and then was told by my psychiatrist that it would be roughly 7 months for titration which was frustrating as you diagnose someone but then tell them they have to wait even longer for medication. I got close to 7 months and nothing so reached out only to be told that it was now a 10-month wait, then got to 10 months and reached out only to be told it was between 10 to 12 months.

I finally reached the 11 month mark at which plan they are supposed to get into contact 28 days before your appointment to line up with the 12 month quoted timeframe, still nothing. So I reached out again to them only to be told by the online advisor that they can't actually give you an accurate time frame even though it's stated on the website.

The people on the web chat are unhelpful, the same as the people operating the telephone lines. The worst thing is they try and fob you off with an excuse about medication shortages but they will happily jump you to queue if you use their paid service. Quite frankly they don't care about the patients at all they care about their profit margins

My diagnosis process was fine, and each of the doctors I've interacted with have been nice, but the overall service is not really fit for purpose. Each patient only gets 12 weeks (!) in titration, how can anyone expect that to be enough time to figure out which medication is right for them, see whether they experience any side effects or not, figure out the right dosage for them, switch medications if the first one or two is not right for them, etc etc. It's just not enough time! Especially when it can take up to 2 weeks for medication to arrive so you have to try and make all of these decisions in advance! From what I understand this rule was not made by Psychiatry UK, but they are providing a service that feels like it doesn't care for it's patients because of that time limit. It feels like you're just being pushed through the system as quickly as possible.
Ironically the system has absolutely no idea how to deal with people with ADHD .

WARNING DO NOT CHOOSE THIS PROVIDER. I was referred to them by my GP for my ADHD assessment and to diagnose me, they only spent 40 minutes asking me some questions about my childhood. Upon my next consultation I was interrupted regularly, not listened to and even had sarcastic comments made to me during my consultation. Upon complaining about this, they responded to this with feeling they had done nothing wrong and offered me no resolution. You will be treated as a tick box exercise.
Terrible service, accessing it was incredibly difficult. Didn't explain to me what I had been referred for and the suddenly sold me that they had closed my case.
Absolutely rubbish. Been waiting 14 months for help. Avoid these at all costs

Need an annual review of my medication which isn’t working. I can’t get an appointment to sort this out for over a year! OVER A YEAR TO REVIEW MEDS!!! Please use another service if you value your sanity.

Abysmal. My first assessment was cancelled with barely 30 minutes' notice. I was sent a link to rebook, but the disruption and lack of regard for patients' time was appalling.

I was eventually assessed on 13th December 2025. It is now late March 2026 and I STILL have not received my report, despite multiple messages through their platform and repeated phone calls. I was promised resolution. Nothing happened. My GP cannot act without this report, so my assessment is effectively meaningless while Psychiatry UK sit on it.

I already have one formal complaint open over the cancelled assessment. If this report isn't with me in the next two weeks, a second will follow.

If you're considering using Psychiatry UK, understand this: getting assessed is only half the battle. Actually getting the paperwork you need, and that your GP needs, to move forward with treatment? Good luck. You'll need it.

If you find yourself in the same position, don't just leave a review. Report your experience to the CQC, complain to NHS England, and contact your MP to escalate to the Parliamentary and Health Service Ombudsman.

one_star_reviews.text:
We got married at St Audries Park in August 2024 and, sadly, our experience after the wedding has completely overshadowed what should have been a special occasion.

Following our wedding, a significant number of our personal belongings were not returned to us, including bespoke wedding items (custom made personalised vow books & A5 signs), gift cards and money (left in the manager’s possession), sentimental keepsakes and decorative items that had been handed over to venue staff.

We were later told that a large box of our belongings had been packed and posted back to us. However, nearly two years on, St Audries Park have still been unable to provide any evidence of this whatsoever — no tracking reference, no courier details, no dispatch confirmation, no proof of contents and no proof of delivery.

Despite repeatedly stating the items were “returned”, they have been unable to show any evidence that they were ever actually sent.

This has been the most frustrating part of the entire process. Had the venue simply accepted responsibility early on and tried to resolve matters properly, this review may have looked very different. Instead, this has involved nearly two years of chasing, repeated delays, contradictory responses and a refusal to provide any meaningful resolution.

What has been most disappointing is not just the loss of our belongings, but how poorly this has been handled since. The tone throughout has felt defensive, dismissive and focused more on avoiding responsibility than resolving the issue fairly. The board of directors have refused in person meetings and phone calls.

For a venue that markets itself as premium and specialises in weddings, we expected much better care, much better communication and much better accountability. We had to pay a £1k deposit which was very slowly returned after repeated chase calls, but the irony is it feels like we should have taken a deposit from St Audries Park for taking possession of our items in the end!

A beautiful venue in photographs, but based on our experience, be extremely cautious about leaving any personal belongings, sentimental items or anything of value in their care. We would not recommend this venue to any new couples.

Very disappointing experience. Prices were not clearly displayed anywhere in the salon, so you cannot check them in advance.

During the service, I asked how much French would be. I was told it’s £10 more, which made me realise I had misunderstood the original price. When I asked again about the total and the infill price, it became clear the cost was much higher than expected.

In general, shellac is usually about £10 more than regular polish — I normally pay around £25 for shellac and about £20 for regular polish elsewhere in London. Here, I was charged £35 for a basic regular polish.

The quality was also poor — uneven application and no basic finishing care like cuticle oil or hand cream. Overall, not good value for money. I would recommend confirming exact prices before starting.

Never leave reviews but unfortunately had to on this occasion. We appreciate that the kind manager managed to get us a walk-in table but he probably should have turned us away as the restaurant seemed to be completely struggling with the amount of customers they had.

We arrived at 6.30 and were finally asked about drinks about 15 minutes later. We decided to put our food order in then as it seemed to be more efficient (and we wanted to help the overrun staff out) but were told it wouldn't come any quicker. We waited about 40 minutes for our drinks, which we reminded our waiter about (and he seemed puzzled that they hadn't already arrived) when he gave us our starter.

The mains came about an hour and a half later, about 4 minutes before we were set to just leave. In that time, several tables just left after being paid no attention to, and several others complained. The food was overpriced for what it was (£23 for a burger, and the bun was burnt), and weirdly, a Pepsi Max cost the same as a Pepsi and a beer (all £6). At no point were we asked about allergies or if we wanted water for the table (despite having glasses).

Just a baffling experience overall. I don't like to complain as I understand it is hard to run a busy restaurant and the waiters were apologetic, but it wasn't exactly packed and the service was so random; we were given menus a second time by a different person even though we had already ordered. They seemed to be out of a lot of options (as other reviews have mentioned) and uncommunicative about wait times: we heard another table who had arrived before us (and who were so unattended to by the staff that we assumed they had finished eating and were just enjoying dessert or something) being told that their food would be another 45 minute wait on top of a 30 minute wait. Just so weird. The manager(?) did give us 10% off though.

So yeah, wouldn't go here again. Would recommend staff don't take walk-ins if they are already struggling with long wait times and tell people upfront what is and isn't available before they commit to a table.

Very Poor experience. An hour wait for food, and then food arriving before drinks. No gluten free options available when we got there despite booking in advance.

Unfortunately, based on our experience, we would not recommend this restaurant.

We visited Catch during our honeymoon in Cornwall after walking for over an hour from Watergate Bay Hotel specifically because we’d seen lobster on the menu and were really looking forward to it. Unfortunately, the experience was extremely disappointing from start to finish.

The first issue was the table location. We were seated in what was essentially a gangway between the kitchen/service area and the toilets. Staff and customers were constantly squeezing past us, the table and drinks shook every time someone brushed by, and people regularly had to stand right next to us to let others pass through. It genuinely didn’t feel like an appropriate place to seat paying customers.

The service was also very poor. Our waitress appeared completely unfamiliar with both the menu and basic customer interaction. We had to prompt her to take our order, she seemed confused by simple drink requests, and after waiting some time another waiter came over to apologise and explain that she hadn’t actually entered our food order at all because she was new.

More concerningly, at no point did anyone ask about allergies, despite this being a seafood restaurant. My wife has a nut allergy, so this is something we would normally expect staff to check routinely as part of basic service and food safety.

At that point we then discovered there was no lobster or crab available, despite these being prominently featured on the menu and the main reason we chose the restaurant. This should have been communicated immediately upon arrival, not after we’d already ordered drinks and starters. Had we known earlier, we would have gone elsewhere.

We ended up ordering fish and chips instead, but were never even told what the “catch of the day” actually was, so we had no idea what fish we were being served. The drinks also arrived in a vase-style container without glasses, which took another several minutes to appear.

The food itself was disappointing too. The batter on the fish was absurdly thick in places (close to 1cm) and very heavy. Both of us ended up peeling large amounts off, and my wife felt quite sick afterwards.

Another thing that really stood out was the salt and pepper presentation. Leaving loose salt in open shells may look aesthetically pleasing, but it’s completely impractical and honestly unhygienic, customers are effectively expected to put their hands into communal seasoning containers, which isn’t something I’d expect at any restaurant.

The only positive was that the whitebait and squid starters were genuinely nice, which is the only reason this isn’t the worst meal we’ve ever had.

Overall, this felt like a restaurant far more focused on appearance and “Instagram aesthetics” than customer comfort, communication, hygiene, safety or food quality. Very disappointing, especially during what was supposed to be a special honeymoon meal.

Visited recently as a local, bringing my dad and stepmum for a treat — it was the first time I’d seen them in over a year. The decor was really lovely and the space itself has a great feel, but unfortunately the overall experience was disappointing.

The main issue was the food not matching what’s described or shown. My linguine (photo attached) was missing multiple key elements (no lemon, pesto, chilli, capers or the advertised dollop of cream) and lacked the expected garlic flavour, quite dry and flavourless. The prawns were also mostly full of roe. My dad’s dish had similar issues — missing components and not resembling what’s advertised at all.
The chowder was the only dish that came close, although even there the prawns were mostly roe. The scallop starters were nice, but lacked any real garlic flavour.

Service was slow despite there being several staff on, (most seemed nervous) and we were the only table of three seated inside for most of the visit. We also had to ask for the main menus after being seated, as only the specials menu was on the table. We had to ask several times for butter, and there was dirty cutlery on the table which needed replacing. One of the toilet doors also had no proper handle.

There were MAJOR issues with the bill. We were initially told 10% had been taken off, which turned out to be the standard local discount, and the scallops were incorrectly priced. After a couple of adjustments (including one that actually increased the bill), it became quite difficult to follow what had been corrected. As a heads up to others, it’s worth checking your bill carefully rather than just paying!!!
The total bill was originally over £100 before the reduction, so this was by no means a cheap meal, and we ended up not staying for desserts due to the experience.

We dined in 2 other places a few days later and had a far better experience food-wise, which highlighted the difference.

The front-of-house staff were pleasant and did try to help although seemed nervous as mentioned above. Overall it felt like things weren’t flowing properly in the kitchen or with billing.

Unfortunately, this experience has put me off returning, which is a shame given the recommendations.

An appalling lack of care and service from the RAC

My 18‑year‑old daughter and her three friends (aged 17–18) broke down at Thorpe Park. They called the RAC at 6pm. No one arrived until midnight. During that time, we discovered that a patrol had been mistakenly sent to Thorpe Park Gardens—over 2.5 hours away. At no point had anyone from the RAC checked or clarified their actual location.
Little care was shown for the fact that four young women were stranded in a vast, deserted car park late at night. I phoned the RAC to explain that they were anxious and felt vulnerable, only to be dismissed with, “What are they worried about?”
When a patrol finally arrived, he immediately confirmed that the car was not drivable—something we had repeatedly told the RAC since 6pm. He also reported that the girls were vulnerable and should be prioritised for transport home. He then left. It was another hour before a taxi arrived. Two taxis refused to take the job because they didn’t want to drive to Wales. During this time, the RAC phone line did not answer our calls, leaving us extremely concerned about how the girls would get home.
The girls were told that someone was on their way to collect the car and were instructed to leave the keys with it. We understood this would be for a short time. However, when they arrived home at 3.45am, the car had still not been collected.
I was repeatedly assured that the car would be recovered before Thorpe Park reopened at 10am. It was not. I alerted the RAC that the car was parked just beyond the exit barrier and would cause an obstruction when the park opened. I also raised concerns about my vehicle being left unattended far longer than I had been told.
Throughout this ordeal, I had to call the RAC multiple times because I was not kept informed. I received contradictory information—at one point I was even told the car had already been collected, which was untrue. I was promised several times that someone from the “special intervention team” would call me. I received only a couple of inadequate text messages, and they did not respond to my replies. I was repeatedly told there was “nothing they could do.”
The car was finally collected at 12pm—42 hours later. I was not informed when it was picked up or when it was delivered to the garage.
The service has been unacceptable on so many levels. The lack of care for my daughter and her friends’ wellbeing and safety was shocking. The disregard for my concerns about my car being left unattended and obstructing an entrance for such a long period was appalling.
This has been the most frustrating and disappointing experience. I have been with the RAC for 30 years, but after this, I will not be renewing my breakdown cover.

4 hours waiting for rescue, 22 minutes on hold waiting to speak to someone, ETA another 4 to 6 hours. What has happened to the RAC? This is a complete scam. There's no other way to describe this utter fiasco. I've paid breakdown premiums on my car insurance for almost 40 years. The amount I've paid must be absolutely staggering but in my hour of need, they're not there. Charlatans. Tomorrow I will cancel my car insurance and take my business elsewhere, anywhere that has no affiliation to the dreadful RAC. If you're breakdown cover is with the RAC, I strongly urge you to make alternative arrangements as soon as possible. Do not put your faith in the RAC. This is fraud as far as I'm concerned. The Financial Conduct Authority should be stepping in to take enforcement action here. Heads should roll, because this is gross mis-selling on a massive scale.

This was a gift voucher given by colleagues for my 60th birthday, so I feel bad as it sounds like I'm ungrateful.
I booked the table 48 hours in advance and gave card details for £20 deposit if we didn't show. I added a note to explain the reason for the visit and also that I was bringing mum after a difficult year in the hope there would be a special welcome as described in a previous review. In the description for the voucher it states:
"Please call us to reserve, so we can make sure we reserve you one of our best tables and have everything ready for your arrival."
I'm not sure why this is the system as the reality was a little more down to earth. There was no indication our table was reserved or that they had read the special request. It was noisy and our table was between the kitchen door, toilet and exit - the door was frequently left open which meant there was a constant draught. The toilet had a wet floor and a child had clearly used it before I did!
Our waiter was lovely - very responsive, polite and helpful.
The food was ok - 2 cheese sandwiches ⭐️ (finger and more pickle and rocket than cheese) 2 ham sandwiches ⭐️⭐️ 2 sausage rolls ⭐️⭐️⭐️, 2 arancinis  (not to our taste )⭐️ 2 cheese tartlets (more chutney than cheese) ⭐️2 scones ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️(lovely and fresh) with cream and jam enough for one, a selection of tray bake cakes which we brought home  - look nice enough, 2 pots of tea and finally 2 fizzy wine which we took away in coffee cups as it was lunchtime and we didn't fancy it.
I think I had higher expectations for £30 per head. When I saw the voucher I pictured table cloths, napkins, and bone china. Instead it was more like a cafe with 3 dying daffodils and a crab cake instead of a scotch egg!
I think it was very overpriced although it has given mum and I a wonderful afternoon out and so much to talk about although perhaps not for the reason intended. The reviews we read were accurate for a motorway service station - there is EV charging, covered bike shed and outdoor wash basins but we were there with very different expectations, maybe because it was our first "Sparkling afternoon tea for two". one_star_reviews.text:
We were quoted nearly £5,000 to put braces on our 15-year-old. The treatment plan letter described her as having a "skeletal jaw discrepancy", "unfavourable growth" and teeth that are "out of sync" with "relatively prominent" front teeth. She is a healthy fifteen-year-old. There is nothing externally wrong with her face. The NHS consultant who gave a second opinion on the same x-ray apparently did not regard her as having a clinical problem of any concern.
The thirteen-page letter opened by assuring us the practice "prides itself on looking after patients as individuals" and described what followed as a "bespoke treatment plan." It then proceeded to spell our daughter's first name incorrectly throughout, and got her mother's surname wrong as well. If "bespoke" doesn't extend to spelling a child's name correctly on her own treatment plan, the word means nothing.
To make matters more peculiar, the practice was happy to take £3,885 to fit her braces, but refused to perform the £1,092 of extractions the same treatment plan required — on the grounds that she couldn't be registered as a patient because her mother isn't registered. Either she is a patient of the practice or she isn't. Quoting for two years of orthodontic care while declining a routine extraction inside the same plan is incoherent.
The thing that bothers me most is the language used in writing about a teenage girl's own face. Teenage girls have plenty to contend with around body image without a private dental practice characterising their appearance as a defect requiring £5,000 to "correct" — particularly when an NHS consultant looking at the same evidence didn't share the level of concern.
My advice to any parent considering this practice: get a referral to an NHS orthodontist first, get a second private opinion from a specialist with no financial stake, and ask to see the actual cephalometric measurements (ANB angle, overjet in mm) before agreeing to anything. The data will tell you whether the framing is justified or whether you're being marketed to.
We took our business elsewhere.

I initially looked into Starlink after a friend recommended it. Their website clearly advertised no upfront costs, with a promotional price of £25 per month for six months, rising to £35 thereafter. Based on that, I decided to make an enquiry.

This feels incredibly misleading. At no point was it made clear that a third party would be involved or that such a significant upfront cost could apply. It gives the impression that customers are being funneled toward expensive installation services that aren’t actually required.

In my opinion, this comes across as a rip-off, and I’d strongly advise others to double-check who they’re dealing with before agreeing to anything. Transparency is seriously lacking here.

would strongly advise anyone considering Easton Bevin Block Management to think very carefully before doing so.

Residents and leaseholders at Pippets Court, Severn Beach, have experienced ongoing issues for a prolonged period, with extremely poor communication and little to no accountability from the management company.

Despite repeated emails, phone calls, and formal complaints from multiple residents, correspondence is routinely ignored. The only consistent communication we seem to receive relates to requests for additional payments and increased management fees, despite longstanding issues remaining unresolved.

One of the biggest concerns has been the ongoing roof problems. Multiple repair attempts have apparently failed over several years, yet leaseholders continue to be asked for further contributions without any clear transparency regarding previous funds or where money has been spent. Serious questions remain unanswered.

Most concerning of all is the impact this has had on residents themselves. An elderly couple at the property were assured repairs above their flat would be completed urgently, yet nothing was done. Their bedroom has since suffered severe water ingress, causing substantial damage and affecting their health and wellbeing. This situation should never have been allowed to happen.

There has also been no AGM for several years, leaving leaseholders without any meaningful opportunity to ask questions or challenge decisions. Transparency appears to be completely lacking.

Meanwhile, basic services continue to decline. Garden maintenance is minimal, communal upkeep is poor, and services such as window cleaning appear to have stopped altogether.

Overall, the level of service provided has been deeply disappointing. Residents are left chasing responses, dealing with unresolved maintenance problems, and facing increasing costs without justification or accountability.

In all honesty, they do not even deserve the one star that has to be given in order to leave this review.

If these issues continue to be ignored and no meaningful response is received, this matter will have to be escalated further with the appropriate authorities. At this stage, residents would even consider pursuing legal action given the lack of communication, accountability, and resolution.

Until there is a significant improvement in communication, transparency, and management standards, I cannot recommend Easton Bevin Block Management.

This was my second visit to the Giggling Squid – Clifton.  My first was about 12 months ago, it was an excellent meal and was the reason for returning whilst staying in Clifton last weekend.  But oh dear, what a contrast.  I can only comment on the two dishes I had, they were really very poor.  The salt and pepper squid, which was spectacularly good 12 months ago, this time consisted of 3-4 big chunks of rubbery squid with not very crispy batter.  Two others in our party also had squid but they had smaller pieces.  They were lacking in flavour with no detectable “salt and pepper” save for a few sliced chillis and spring onions.  Worst of all was the accompanying sauce/dip.  No idea how this was made, but it seemed like a cheap tomato ketchup mixed with sweet chilli sauce, then a few sliced chillis chucked in to try and improve the appearance. It was glutinous and quite unpleasant, certainly like nothing I have encountered before.  As it was now 9:30, an hour after we arrived, I did eat  all the squid, but not the sauce.

The main course was a Massaman curry.  This did not taste of much, but it was not very pleasant and again, it was unlike any massaman I have ever encountered.  Only ate about a third of it, left most of the rice as mixing it with the sauce – usually a pleasure with any Thai curry was just not nice.  At the end of the meal when the plates were being cleared, I did mention to the waiter that it was not very pleasant which was why most of my meal was left, he did apologise, but nothing more.

Looking at the other reviews, many 5 stars,  it seems my experience was the exception rather than the rule.  Whilst the cooking and seasoning of the squid could be put down to just one of those things at the end of a busy night, the unpleasantness of the sauce/dip and the quality of the Massaman curry are less easy to explain away.

I do hope that this is not a result of a deliberate policy of putting up prices and reducing costs by using cheaper ingredients.  Unfortunately, this is not unusual if new private equity partners in a business are trying to increase short term profitability before selling on their share of the business.  I hope I’m wrong, but I would need some persuading to ever return again – sorry.

I am not one to usually write reviews, however my experience with DLG Legal Services has been absolutely abysmal.

I was involved in a road traffic accident in late 2021 and, nearly five years later, my claim still remains unresolved despite the other driver admitting liability very early on. Throughout that time I have experienced repeated delays, multiple case handler changes and long periods with little meaningful communication or progress.

The most distressing issue, however, was the disclosure of a psychological report containing highly sensitive personal information. Medical and family-related information relating to myself and a family member was disclosed to someone who absolutely should not have received it, and the document was not adequately redacted. Additionally, said family member was also a completely separate data subject who was not involved in the claim and should not have been included in the report at all. The report contained deeply private information, including mental health history and family matters, which caused significant distress when disclosed.

I raised a formal complaint and provided detailed concerns, yet months later I am still waiting for a proper response addressing the issues raised. When I chased for a response to my complaint, I was told I was welcome to refer the matter to the Legal Ombudsman rather than receiving a substantive response. Being left to chase answers about both my claim and my complaint has only added to the frustration.

After years of delays, poor communication and the handling of sensitive information, I have lost complete confidence in the service provided. This has been an extremely stressful and disappointing experience.
Very unprofessional in their handling of a claim. Hope they go out of business and leave this to the professionals.

I had a very disappointing experience with DLG Legal Services. Communication was slow and inconsistent, which made an already stressful situation even worse. I often had to chase for updates, and when I did get responses, they weren’t always clear or helpful.
I also felt that my case wasn’t given the attention or urgency it deserved. The service came across as quite impersonal, and I didn’t feel properly supported or guided through the process.

I do not usually leave reviews or complaints, which should show how serious this situation has become. However, after my experience with DLG Legal Services, I feel compelled to warn others and formally express how unacceptable their handling of my case has been.

At 18 years old, I was involved in a road traffic collision caused by a drunk driver while returning home from a night shift. I suffered physical injuries, significant emotional distress, loss of my vehicle, loss of independence, and the wider impact of the incident also affected my employment. This was an extremely difficult period of my life, and I relied on DLG Legal Services to represent my interests professionally and efficiently.

Review Title: $250 Lost, 3 Months of Excuses — I Had to File a Claim to Get My Money Back
I’ve been a loyal Foxy Locks customer for years, spending thousands annually, but this last experience has completely ended that relationship. I paid $250 for merchandise that I never received, and instead of stepping in as a responsible business should, Foxy Locks :Josie left me in limbo for over three months.
She repeatedly told me the package was being “held” at DHL and that only I, the customer, could resolve it. That’s absurd. As the recipient, I had no authority to search DHL warehouses, no access to their systems, and no ability to make DHL release a package they themselves couldn’t locate. But trust me, I tried I dealt with DHL reps, supervisors anybody up the chain of command I could. In reality, the parcel was lost. Period. But instead of acknowledging this and taking responsibility, Foxy Locks chose to hide behind policy.
One line from their emails summed it up: they said refunding me while the package was “available” would have been a risk. Risk? The only risk here was leaving me, the paying customer, with no product and no money. Whether they refunded me or sent a replacement, the company’s position would have been the same — down one order. But instead of protecting their loyal customer, they chose to protect themselves.
And here’s what makes it worse: I didn’t get my refund because Foxy Locks decided to do the right thing. I got my money back because I filed a claim against them and won. That’s not customer service — that’s being forced to fight for what was already mine.
Only after I said I was taking this public did someone else step in and offer a “20% discount.” At that point, it was laughable, not only do they want my continued business. This one might get lost too, and then I’ll be out twice the amount of money not to mention 20% off there overpriced product is nothing at all. Their product and quality is not as good as Luxy.They had three months to offer a refund, a replacement, or even a small gesture of goodwill. They offered nothing until their reputation was on the line.
Policies don’t excuse poor ethics. And if Foxy Locks refuses to back up shipments when DHL fails, they shouldn’t be using DHL at all. The truth is simple: Foxy Locks put the entire burden on me, the customer, and washed their hands of it, merely saying sorry for your inconvenience and doing nothing about it.

Experience:
Calling up enquiring a gym tour -
After browsing the Bristol Riverside Gym website there was an icon that says “Register your interest for a free gym tour here:” so I entered my name and email and didn’t hear back for a day. I thought this was odd as most gym sign ups usually have an automated follow up email like “click to book a tour date” or “come to this address for your tour.”

So I called the Bristol centre and the receptionist was so reluctant to talk to me. The conversation went like this:

Me: “Hi, can I book for a tour today?”
Receptionist: “You don’t need to.”
Me: “Oh ok, please may I come in today and look around.”
Receptionist: “Ok”
Me: “Ok…should I turn up whenever I like?”
Receptionist: “Yes.”
Me: “Sure, thank you I’ll see you today”
Receptionist: “Ok”

Gym tour -
Upon arrival:
I was pointed at to sit down. Whilst receptionist was on a private call.

Tour guide (same receptionist) was reluctant to speak about the equipment and the benefits of the gym. But when I asked “when is it a good time to use the studio?” I was told I can only use it if I’m a member (seemed like an obvious understanding for me) so I proceeded to ask “could I use this any time of the day after joining?” and the tour guide responded with “ you can only use it if you’re a member.” My impression was that they didn’t think I was being serious and a time waster. It’s worth mentioning throughout the tour I was complimentary of the space, lots of room and variety of equipment and politely said please and thank you.

Signing up for a new membership -

After the tour I thought to myself I’m committed to being active and trialling out a new local gym despite the whole experience already because, I wanted to keep my positive mindset going. How wrong I was to sign up to the gym…

After the tour I said to the tour guide “this gym looks great, please could I sign up for a membership” and their response was “you can do that online.” I thought that’s not a problem, I wanted to start straight after the gym tour so thought signing up in person was more effective. My response to the receptionist was “Ok I guess I’ll open the website here and join right now, do you need any details from me because I want to start right now.” The receptionist was adamant that I “just sign up online” and that was it.

Later on I read through my sign up email and there was a list of expectations from the gym:

- I needed a code to scan into the gym.
- I had to show the receptionist my sign up so they could set me up on the access system.
- And generally I expected an induction of some sort…anything really. Seemed to be the process for most places I’ve been to.

So that was my first day experience, after I signed up, I walked myself around until I found what I needed.

Other experiences:
25th Mar At the entrance there wasn’t any revolving gates so anyone could stroll in without a membership or if they thought they fancied to observe others at the gym - this felt very unsafe to me. And as a paying customer you wouldn’t want to risk this or think “why am I paying a membership if anyone can stroll in?”

Secondly, two distinct things to point out in the gym:

The women’s only gym has the ceiling completely open, you can see the wiring and water leakages - looks like a construction site. Plus the equipment in the women’s room was very old and rusty - not a problem if there was an induction on how to use the equipment or as I did, try and find out…if a heavy weight falls on your head or foot, if the chair isn’t securely fastened and breaks your back - who cares…am I right Bristol gym?

And I had the lovely observation of watching a man in the pool phlegm up from his throat and spit into the swimming pool and lock eye contact with me in silence. I wasn’t going to look but having heard the sounds of him working up the phlegm…I think it’s hard to not try look around and figure out “who’s doing that?” Enjoy swimming there :)

I’ve never returned since that day. I could probably count up to 10-15 issues I had and still gave it my positive spirit. BIG MISTAKE!

Emailed 3x

one_star_reviews.text:
We hired a campervan from Hi De Hi Campers in October 2025. During this rental period, we liaised with the owner, Russell Marsden directly over WhatsApp.

Pros:
The booking and handover process was smooth. Russell gave a thorough walkthrough of the vehicle, and the campervan served its intended purpose for our trip. There were pre-existing issues (for example, a broken window signal light), and we were reassured these would not be charged to us. We were also told that reasonable wear and tear from normal use was expected. In hindsight, these reassurances were misleading, as the post-hire process revealed serious issues.

Cons:
We chose this company based on its positive reviews, but we were left disappointed. The post-hire damage handling was extremely poor. During our trip, a minor scratch appeared on the table surface. At handover, we were told assessment would take about a week. Instead, we had to chase for updates from October 2025 until 2 March 2026 — nearly five months later — and we are still waiting for complete paperwork regarding the issue. Documentation was severely lacking, and Russell’s communication was poor; he repeatedly avoided providing requested information.

Russell insisted the entire table must be replaced for a single scratch and made this decision before properly considering repair. He could not even get a quotation or response from the supplier, yet replacement remained the proposed solution.

Additional unverified damages were also attempted for deduction from our deposit. The standard deposit for hirers is around £1,000–£1,250, but we were asked to pay more on the basis that we were from out of state. While different risk policies may apply, this felt disproportionate and exploitative. Furthermore, Russell told us that cash payment was preferred for part of the proposed damage cost, with comments suggesting this is what business people do for tax-related reasons, raising serious concerns.

Overall, the lack of transparency, misleading reassurances, prolonged delays, poor communication, and questionable handling of the damage claim severely overshadowed the hire. While the campervan itself worked as intended, the post-hire experience has been frustrating and stressful.

We strongly advise prospective customers to ensure all deposit terms, damage assessment policies, payment methods, and timelines are clearly documented in writing before hiring from this company.

It is extremely disappointing that something that was meant to be a positive experience is ruined by a dealer like Russell...

Decided to go into Starbucks at Indian Queens/Fraddon today whilst shopping. On arrival, I waited to order and the till operator was kind and helpful.

My mother and I sat at a table closest to the collection area (we were drinking in), as it was clearly within earshot. An Americano arrived after about 5 minutes, which was slightly slow but understandable given there was a queue. However, like others waiting, our drinks were coming out in a random order (not together). I then waited a further 10 minutes (minimum) for mine, despite there only being around 6–8 customers waiting at any time and three staff behind the counter.

The wait itself wasn’t the main issue. After around 15 minutes, I politely asked a member of staff if she knew how long my drink would be. I was told, “yours is up next, probably,” following a very quick, dismissive glance at the tickets. I couldn’t confidently say that she genuinely read the tickets.

When I explained it had already been quite a long wait, the response became unnecessarily abrupt. The staff member gestured to the space around her and said, “well we clearly don’t have much room here,” before turning her back on me. This came across as defensive and unprofessional, especially since I made the effort to approach the situation sincerely.

After a few moments I was then told that there was no ticket for my order and told that I had to return to the till to verify my purchase. At this point, I felt offended that the member of staff considered that my query could be an attempt to con the store. It was one coffee for an order that already been half delivered. Perhaps the member of staff wanted to see my order details for the purpose of seeing if there was any modifications, allergies etc., which would have been a plus for service, but given the manner displayed, I very much doubt it.

The entire interaction took place in full view of other customers, which made the experience more uncomfortable. I was close to challenging the way I was being spoken to, but chose not to escalate it.

To top it off, another customer then pointed out that my drink had already been made and was sitting on the counter waiting to be handed over.

Delays happen but this review really comes down to the how rude and offensive this interaction was. What’s more, just a basic level of attentiveness and courtesy would have prevented the situation entirely.

one_star_reviews.text:
If you’re considering dropping serious money on Loaf products, you may want to read this review before you make your decision to use Loaf. I’ve always had Loaf up as one of the premium UK brands for beds, furniture and homeware, but this experience changed that.

For context, we’ve bought many Loaf sofas and beds in the past and been very happy, so decided to pay £1.2k for a Kingsize “muffin top” mattress. We always knew there was cheaper products out there, but we value that a premium brand like Loaf normally means a first class service if there’s any issues. These beds are handmade to order, so it takes 4-6 weeks for the mattress to arrive. We were happy to wait and we sold our old mattress the night before the delivery, so we were ready and excited for our brand new mattress.

It arrived and within minutes of us unpacking the mattress, our excitement turned to disappointment. The mattress appears soiled and used. We had bought and paid full price for a brand new mattress, but it had multiple black marks on, what appears to be foundation/make-up marks and the thread on the mattress was pulled. Then in addition to the soiled mattress, Loaf had actually sown into the mattress the complete wrong product label. In big bold letters, it’s stitched in saying this is a “Top Dog” mattress, but the mattress made to order is clearly a “Muffin Top” mattress. This means if we want to sell this on in the future, we can’t even sell it as a “Muffin Top”.

We reached out to Loaf and they promised they’d respond within 24 hours, as it was urgent and we were currently sleeping on a soiled mattress. After 24 hours, we’d heard nothing and then they responded 8 days later and they offered less than 10% off and we keep the mattress.

Or they could try to exchange it but it may take another 6 weeks to make another mattress up, so we’d have to sleep on a soiled mattress until then.

They did mention they could send a team out to try clean it, but it would invalidate the warranty for anything to do with the condition of the mattress and it wouldn’t be restored to brand new, so we wouldn’t be entitled to any compensation for being sent a soiled mattress.

We’ve been really happy with Loaf over the years, but this experience has left us with a sour taste. We’re environmentally-conscious, so would hope we could find a suitable solution, where we keep the mattress, get it professionally cleaned, keep the warranty and have a reasonable offer to compensate us for having to use a soiled mattress, but it doesn’t appear that Loaf are able to find a suitable solution. We really hoped, when things went wrong, they would go above and beyond to make things right, but that sadly hasn’t happened.

I’m gutted I’m having to write this review, but if you want premium service and a premium product, I would recommend looking elsewhere unfortunately. I’ll update this review if anything changes in Loaf’s response.

one_star_reviews.text: I was on the receiving end of call about a ghost job where they asked for personal information about previous managers. Clearly data harvesting and a very immoral thing to do. Fortunately I figured things out right away.

Review Title: Data Mining Disguised as Recruitment – Avoid.
Rating: ⭐☆☆☆☆
I am writing this to warn other professionals about the unethical practices I experienced with Tank Recruitment, specifically an agent named Harrison.
I was cold-called regarding a contract role (Outside IR35, £200–£280/day). Before providing any concrete details about the company, the location, or the specific JD, Harrison insisted on 3-4 professional references. Thinking this was a fast-moving requirement, I provided them.
The Reality:
* Zero follow-up: Within 24 hours, he had contacted every single one of my references.
* Radio silence: Despite my references giving glowing feedback, Harrison vanished. He provided no information on the "client" or the interview process.
* The "Pivot": After I called him twice for an update, his story shifted. When I mentioned I had another interview elsewhere, he immediately told me to "go ahead with that one" because it was "likely a no" for his role.
The Red Flag:
It became glaringly obvious that there was likely no job to begin with. This was a textbook "reference mining" exercise—using a candidate’s data to build a network of hiring managers to pitch to. It’s essentially a pyramid scheme of information-gathering where the candidate is just the bait.
Fortunately, I have a strong relationship with my references, and I have since advised them to block all contact from Tank Recruitment. If you value your professional reputation and your references' time, do not give this company any information until you have a verified interview in writing.
Audacious, unprofessional, and a total waste of time.
A Quick Tip for Next Time
To protect your network, you might want to adopt a "References available upon successful interview/offer" policy. A legitimate recruiter will almost never need to speak to your current or past bosses before you've even seen a job description.

I’ve had a pretty frustrating experience with Cuckoo Fibre overall, despite some positives.

To start with the good: when the connection actually works, the speeds are genuinely very good. Streaming, downloads, and general browsing are all fast and stable at times, which is what you’d hope for from a fibre provider.

However, the issues around everything else have really let it down.

Customer service has been a major pain point. It often feels like the support team doesn’t fully understand what’s being asked, even for relatively simple requests. On multiple occasions, I’ve tried to get straightforward changes made and it’s either taken far too long or hasn’t been done correctly at all.

A big limitation is the lack of control over the router. You can’t make basic network changes yourself — things like opening ports, changing the WiFi password, or even renaming your network. This is incredibly restrictive, especially if you have smart home devices, gaming setups, or anything that requires port forwarding or custom configuration. Most providers allow at least some level of user control, so this feels unnecessarily locked down.

I’ve also had ongoing issues with devices struggling to connect reliably. There have been multiple engineer visits, and while they’ve confirmed there is a problem, no one seems able to identify the root cause. To make matters worse, the engineers aren’t directly employed by Cuckoo, so there’s a bit of a disconnect in accountability and follow-up.

On the administrative side, things haven’t been much better. I submitted a subject access request over 2.5 months ago and am still waiting for a response, which is well beyond expected timeframes. Formal complaints also seem to disappear into a void — I’m told responses have been sent, but I’ve never actually received them.

In summary, while the raw internet speeds are strong, the lack of router control, poor customer support, unresolved technical issues, and slow (or nonexistent) responses to formal requests make this a difficult service to recommend.

We had a table booked at The Golden Heart Winterbourne for 7:15pm on 1st May 2026 for a birthday celebration. There were three adults. We ordered our food just before 7:30pm, along with drinks, which took around 15 minutes to arrive.

By around 8:10pm, we still hadn’t received our food, despite noticing other tables around us being served — including a nearby table already being offered dessert menus and another with their dessert. We called a waitress over to ask for an update. She briefly spoke to a colleague, appeared visibly frustrated, huffing then returned and told us it would be “5 minutes.” It was at this point we thought she hadn’t put our order through.

Unfortunately, 15 minutes passed with no food. When we asked again, we were told it “wouldn’t be long,” and only at that point did we receive an apology. We then asked to speak to the manager, who came over roughly 10 minutes later who was polite and repeated that the food wouldn’t be long, offering 50% off as compensation and said sorry again. Which was kind but we were hungry and frustrated we had to call over to the waitress to even ask for an update. No one had even asked us if we wanted more drinks.

After explaining the situation, we asked directly whether our order had been missed. The manager then confirmed that although the waitress had entered the order into the iPad, she hadn’t actually sent it through to the kitchen. While we understand that mistakes happen, it was disappointing that this wasn’t communicated honestly from the start. Being told “5 minutes” when the order hadn’t even been processed felt misleading. If at that point we were told the truth we could have decided for ourselves if we wanted to wait.

At that stage, with no clear idea of when our food would arrive and after waiting until around 8:30pm, we decided to leave. Overall, the experience was frustrating due to the lack of communication and transparency, rather than the mistake itself. Better honesty and proactive updates would have made a significant difference. It’s human nature to make a mistake but honestly is better.

We commissioned Pestology for an expensive CCTV drainage survey (£350) to identify exactly how rats were entering our property. Their website claims an evidence-led approach that pinpoints entry routes, but in reality, the service was unprofessional, contradictory, and completely failed to deliver what was promised.

Specific failings include:
CCTV images were blurry, unclear, and often unidentifiable, with no video footage provided, making it impossible to verify any conclusions.

One image in our report was of a drain at another address which is ridiculous!

The surveyor concluded that a displaced joint was the likely rat entry point, yet the owner later stated this was unlikely and that it was due to a "possible" redundant pipe. This was not mentioned on the day of the survey and this was speculation with no evidence.

Numerous basic factual inaccuracies: electric and gas boxes mislabelled as external, references to manholes not on the map. Drainage map was incorrect and no exact identification of where the the new manhole should be. Any drainage company who carry out CCTV reports would provide this. The report should be understood by any drainage company and I have had many companies shocked with the quality of this report along with the price.

Several areas were marked as inspected but were not checked, including burrow points, extension gaps, and patio edges. Felt like pictures of the property were being taken for the sake of it but no real external inspection as promised.

They offered a second survey of which I thought my concerns would at least be communicated and basic checks finally done. However, the second surveyor was rude, unprofessional, and unaware it was a follow-up survey, leaving a pipe uncapped behind the toilet, creating a hygiene risk and another entry point. No external checks were made and we were not provided with a new report that was corrected. Instead we were given pages and pages of more blurry images and told no conclusion could be made until manhole was installed. Of which this work was quoted at approx £3500. No accountability was taken by the owner, instead assumptions were made as to why we took the survey (apparently to get money back from the seller).

Overall failures:
After two surveys, we still do not know for certain how rats are entering the property.
The CCTV surveys did not add any useful information beyond what we already knew from a prior Thames Water inspection.
The recommended “manhole” was completely unnecessary to tell us what we already knew — we had communicated the lack of a manhole at the start.
Despite claiming an evidence-led, forensic approach, they could not provide clear evidence, proper analysis, or actionable findings, and instead pushed for expensive remedial works which we already knew needed to be done.
In short, this was an expensive, misleading, and unprofessional service that failed to provide the basic purpose of a CCTV survey: clear, reliable, and evidenced findings. Pestology’s claims about pinpointing entry routes and delivering evidence-led recommendations are utterly misleading. We would not recommend them for any drainage or pest inspections. You are better off using a drainage company for the CCTV report. If they can't provide what they promised with the report or take any accountability for the poor quality, inaccuracies and contradictions, then they cannot expect customers to spend such a large sum of money trusting that they will do any job well. We were happy to part with the £3500 if they did their job well but unfortunately accuracy, quality and care does not seem to be important to pestology. We are just one of the 30 visits they do a day.

I hate leaving a negative review. Two years on, I've tried to fall in love with this car and I haven't.

Porsche Bristol had my perfect spec in stock: a Taycan Turbo S. We negotiated, secured the car, and two weeks later I was ready to collect.

Knowing we had a four hour drive each way, I called two days in advance to confirm collection time and that everything was prepped and ready. I was told it was.

Spoilers: It wasn't.

We arrived to find the car hadn't been prepped, serviced, MOT'd or signed off. Before I'd even had a proper look at my new pride and joy, the car was sent straight into the workshop.

What should have been a wonderful 60 minute handover turned into a full day. My partner, my dog and I sat around for hours, hungry and tired. Very little was done to look after us beyond being told to go and grab some lunch.

We left late in the evening with the car and the accessories. Got home about 2am the next day, went to charge it, and discovered the wrong charger and cabling had been supplied. No charging.

A few days later the car began throwing errors and wouldn't go into drive, it was a paperweight on my driveway. My local Porsche dealer arranged collection and after inspecting the car told me the battery casing had concerning damage and two tyres were at their legal limits. None of which had been flagged during handover.

What followed was a painful process with Porsche Bristol to put it all right. Not smooth. Not easy. Nowhere near the elegant experience I'd expected from the brand. They took very little ownership.

This week Porsche Bristol called to ask if I'd be interested in a new car. Their handling of the sale, and everything after, has put me off the brand entirely. I'm now in the process of selling it.

Things go wrong. That's fine. It's how a brand responds when they do that defines them, and the response here was very, very poor.

Please do better. Maybe one day I'll come back to Porsche.

Beware, raw meat in the burger, high risk of food poisoning.

Love Almondsbury Garden Center but this time I was badly surprised in the café. I ordered burger with chips and after eating 3/4 of the burger I looked at the meat in the middle and it was… raw. I’ve alerted staff member who called another staff member to my table and she offered a refund due to the burger being not up to my satisfaction, not to being unsafe. She took the remainder of it and came back saying the chef said it was fine, you can safely eat undercooked burger meat.

I’m greatly concerned how lightly they’ve treated this, saying nothing will happen and I’ll be fine.

If the meat was contaminated with bacteria like E. coli or Salmonella, symptoms typically take 1 to 5 days to appear, though they can start in as little as 6 hours. So I guess I have to wait and see what happens.

No, it is never safe to eat undercooked burger meat. Even if you have eaten it before without getting sick, ground beef always carries a high risk of food poisoning. Unlike a steak, where harmful bacteria stay on the outside surface, the process of grinding meat mixes those bacteria all the way through the center of the patty. The only way to destroy them completely is to cook the meat to an internal temperature of 71C.

One would think a professional chef would know that.

That’s it. Ate there 7 hours ago. Waiting to see if I get ill or not.

Rating: 1/10
​This review is a formal documentation of the systemic failures I have experienced regarding my daughter’s welfare and the complete lack of professional accountability from the authorities involved.
​Key Failures and Logical Inconsistencies:
​Violation of Accessible Communication: Despite having documented disabilities and a formal request for direct telephone contact, this agency deliberately used email as a primary contact method. This is a direct failure to provide reasonable adjustments and ensure both parties were properly notified.
​Procedural Delay & Court Intervention: It took over six months for required documents to be produced. The delay was so severe that the Court had to intervene and order immediate production. This level of negligence in a family law matter is unacceptable.
​Substitution of Assumption for Medical Fact: Rather than conducting a thorough investigation of medical records, the agency based life-altering recommendations on clinical assumptions. This resulted in a "one-size-fits-all" demand for therapy, ignoring the fact that I was already engaged in professional support and have documented histories of PTSD, BPD, and ADHD from 2016.
​Inequality of Accountability: The system claims to prioritize the child’s relationship with both parents, yet it allowed a 12-year-old to make an adult-level decision regarding no-contact based on a "brainwashed" situation. Pretty disappointed with how this event is handled overall. It just feels a bit all over the place, and communication isn’t great, which makes things more frustrating than they need to be.

The ticket situation is a bit of a pain as well. If your plans change, there’s not much flexibility, and actually passing tickets on isn’t as straightforward as you’d expect. Tickets aren’t cheap for most people either, so being stuck with them when something comes up is a pretty big issue.

Tried reaching out to Rock Oyster Festival 2026 for some help but didn’t hear anything back, which didn’t exactly help the situation. It seems like getting a response can be a bit hit and miss.

On top of that, it doesn’t always feel like great value for money — queues can be long, it gets pretty crowded, and some of the basic stuff doesn’t quite keep up with the number of people there.

Overall, it’s a nice idea and the setting is great, but the way it’s run just doesn’t quite live up to expectations.

Had to pull out of attending this event unexpectedly, which is unfortunate but one of those things. What’s been far more disappointing is how difficult it is to pass tickets on.

The event’s website points you toward using Tixel as the official resale route, but in practice that doesn’t really work. You can’t actually list anything without a PDF ticket, and those aren’t issued until right before the event. By then, it’s unrealistic to expect anyone to buy them.

Tried getting in touch with Rock Oyster Festival 2026 for some guidance, but didn’t hear anything back. That lack of communication just adds to the frustration.

As it stands, there doesn’t seem to be any practical way to recover the cost once plans change, which feels like a pretty significant gap in the process.

I purchased £450 worth of tickets for the 2026 event but am unfortunately no longer able to attend. While I understand and accept the no-refund policy, the lack of a workable resale option has been very frustrating.

The Rock Oyster website directs customers to use the authorised resale platform, Tixel. However, Tixel requires a PDF version of the tickets in order to list them, and Rock Oyster does not issue these until one week before the event. This effectively prevents any realistic opportunity to resell tickets in advance.

I have contacted Rock Oyster twice to seek clarification or assistance and have not received any response. As things stand, I appear to have no viable option other than to absorb the full £450 loss.

Given the lack of response to direct enquiries, leaving a review feels like the only way to highlight this issue and seek some form of resolution.

Very dishonest organisers: when headliner Sophie Ellis-Bextor cancelled they just put a random dj instead without offering any compensation as every other festival does. When I contacted them on Facebook regarding it they blocked me. Definitely don't recommend.

I am writing to raise serious concerns about the care I received at Lawrence Hill Health Centre, particularly from Dr Charles Dixon.

Following this, my condition worsened severely. I experienced extreme insomnia for five consecutive days and uploaded my prescription to the practice system, requesting guidance. I received no response. As my condition escalated, I was forced to attend emergency services twice. The hospital also contacted the GP practice regarding my situation, yet I was not followed up.

On attending the practice again, despite an emergency appointment being recorded in my name, I was turned away without appropriate care or assessment.

This lack of timely intervention and support led to a critical deterioration in my mental health, culminating in a hospitalisation due to an overdose — a situation that could have been fatal.

The following day, Dr Dixon contacted me again but remained dismissive, did not allow me to speak, and showed no acknowledgement or sensitivity towards the fact that I had just experienced a suicide attempt. Instead, I was blamed for seeking medication advice externally.

This experience reflects a serious failure in duty of care, communication, and patient safety. I believe the handling of my case was negligent and could have resulted in loss of life.

I urge the practice to review its procedures for handling mental health crises, improve patient communication, and ensure that urgent cases receive appropriate and timely care.

The first thing you say is I absolutely love the dog we got just under 2 years ago from Willowtimle.

Although I have to really be honest about the issues we’ve had. We’ve seen 3 different trainers and our dog is so intelligent. However in seeing all of them they all have been very shocked at the issues we’ve had - digestion, overactivity, reactivity and all of them think this most likely comes from the early treatment with the puppies. Talking to a behaviourist they were shocked about the amount of gut issues she has had, and 2 other people I know who have got litters from Willowtimle of different ages have had the same issues.

The puppies just don’t get the handling and socialisation they need at a young age. They live outside, mum is often not around once they are a bit older, they don’t do any socialisation. They don’t really care who takes the puppies, we clearly didn’t have any experience and the main question was around securing the dog.

I would say my dog is probably one of the most intelligent and gorgeous dogs going and she is so liked by everyone. But I finally 2 years later feel like I really need to share.

When we got a puppy we were reading about if we got our dog from a puppy farm. We thought it couldn’t be like that, good reviews, kennel club approved. But I have to reflect and say perhaps we did.

Did a trial shift here, they use shock collars on the youngsters, they muzzle boarding dogs (a dog called HERO was there at the time, they were screaming at him to “shut up” and when he didn’t they put a fabric muzzle on him to stop him opening his mouth), when a dog didn’t listen correctly to a command they grabbed the dog by their throat and dragged them back inside the paddock. I reported this back to Honey the manager and got no response. This has all been reported to the appropriate channels.

Breakdown at Gordano Services after losing all caravan rear lights—turned out to be a blown fuse. Green Flag sent Westbourne Motors, and while the response time was quick, everything after that went downhill.

The recovery driver was polite but clearly inexperienced. I explained upfront that it was likely just a fuse (I’m a retired mechanic with breakdown experience), but he ignored that and insisted on stripping out my entire boot—awning, mobility scooter, everything—only to say he couldn’t find anything. He then made no effort to check the main fuse box where I suggested.

Instead, he decided to tow the caravan back to storage. I even suggested a low loader would be more suitable, but this was ignored. Two hours later, in the dark, wind, and rain, he finally arrived. We quickly unhitched and moved the caravan ourselves.

Within minutes of him leaving, we found damage to the caravan (front and rear offside). This was reported immediately to Green Flag with clear photographic evidence, including a photo showing no damage before towing. Despite this, Westbourne Motors are now claiming the evidence isn’t good enough.

To make matters worse, when I called Westbourne Motors directly to try and resolve things without insurance, the attitude I received was sarcastic and dismissive as soon as I explained who I was.

At this point, it feels like constant buck-passing and avoidance. Based on this experience, I think Green Flag should seriously reconsider using Westbourne Motors. There are plenty of reliable, professional recovery companies out there—this isn’t one of them.

We recently visited this farm as a family of four. When booking tickets, we were prompted to add animal feed, and it gave the impression that different types of feed were needed for different animals. We ended up purchasing all of them, but this wasn’t actually the case. Even the lady at reception mentioned that the website hasn’t yet been updated to reflect this correctly.

As we entered the park, we immediately noticed how run-down it looked. Our first stop was the soft play area, where much of the equipment was either broken or out of order.

As we continued around the park, it became clear that the further in you go, the worse the condition becomes. The animals seemed extremely hungry — it was difficult to even get the feed out of the bag before they were grabbing it from over the fences.

There were ride-on tractors on a track, but again, many of these were broken to the point they could have been unsafe. The same applied to several other rides and attractions, which were either out of order or in poor condition.

We also found that many of the hand-washing stations didn’t work, and the ones that did had very little water coming out.

We made the best of our visit and still managed to have a fun few hours, but having paid £60 for a family of four, we don’t feel this was reasonable value considering the overall state of the farm.

For the money they make from visitors they need to start spending it on the venue before it will close for good.

Awful experience. The photographer's behaviour was extremely rude and unprofessional. It all started when we received a free baby photo shoot experience through bounty. After the photo shoot we were told we would need to book another appointment to view the photos and he asked us to take a photo of the pricelist.

Next time we arrived we were 5 minutes early and he showed us to the viewing room. We selected a few photos to take away and asked the photographer if he could offer a discount as the prices were quite frankly out of our budget. Then he immediately raised his voice and in a rude and insulting tone of voice berated us on how he needs to pay the landlord and feed his family. My baby was forced to witness this. He didn't need to go into length about why he was charging his prices, he could've said a simple yes or no instead of trying to make us all feel guilty. I've attached the photo of the pricelist to show that our ask wasn't unreasonable. He used the example of asking for a discount at tesco suggesting that was unreasonable but in fact tesco do discounts through their club card scheme and promotions. The photographer said he would contact us when the print was ready. We left the studio shaken and offended.

We would not recommend this photographer and reading other positive reviews, we believe we were not treated equally. The photos were not well photographed either. What would've helped was if we were provided the pricelist well in advance then we would've decided if the photoshoot was worth our time. We waited over a month (how long would a small photo take to print?), we received no contact so that all was a complete waste of everyone's time.

Avoid UK Carbody Ltd in Avonmouth, Bristol

Excellent Bodywork, Atrocious Administration and Communication
I wish I could give this review two separate scores: one for the actual bodywork repair and one for everything else. Unfortunately, the “everything else” has been so bad that it completely overshadows the good parts.

The quality of the bodywork repair and valet was excellent. The panels, paint, and finish were done to a very high standard – no complaints there at all.
However, the administration, communication, and overall service have been truly atrocious.

My wife has been without her car since the end of January after our insurance company instructed UK Carbody Ltd to carry out the repairs following an accident.

•  We were told to drive the car to their premises for inspection, my wife thought the loud noise when driving was air passing through the hole in the door. So thought it was safe to drive.

•  After the first inspection, they contacted us to say it needed to be done again because the original one wasn’t completed correctly.

•  When dropping the car off for repair I told told her that the noise she suspected to be air sounded more like a wheel bearing. My wife specifically mentioned that she suspected the noise was a wheel bearing and was told not to worry they will check everything. They diagnosed the bodywork as “cost effective” to repair.

•  The bodywork was repaired and the car valeted beautifully, but the loud noise from the wheel bearing remained exactly the same after the accident. We reported it immediately.

•  UK Carbody then said the bearing is noise was “age related” because the car is 10 years old. This ignores the fact that the car had done only 50,000 miles, VW states wheel bearings typically last around 100,000 miles, none of the other bearings have failed, and crucially – there was no noise at all before the accident.

The car is now off the road and unroadworthy. We have had to escalate this through the insurance ombudsman and involve legal representation.

If your insurance company directs you to use UK Carbody Ltd for repairs, do not accept it without serious hesitation. Insist on an alternative repairer if possible. The visual repair work may be excellent  but the complete lack of proper process, communication, and willingness to address related damage makes the whole experience a nightmare.

I would not recommend this company based on our experience.
