I took my Canon G7X camera into the shop after dropping it and the lense would not retract back into the camera- so it stopped functioning.

When I first initially dropped this camera, it was around the 19th of March, however I only decided to take it to a camera repair store on the 27th of March (see attached). I then received the quote on the 2nd of April and decided to look for alternatives, so I picked the camera up on the 7th of April and brought it to Camera city where it was booked.

Upon collecting it on the 15th of April,  there had been discoloration to the screen, there was vertical lines going down the camera and discoloration of purple, something I have never seen on the camera before since dropping it. When I went and took it back to them after realizing they stated that it was because I dropped it that the "crystals" in the screen must have leaked. But after getting second opinions from other camera shops they told me that if I did damage the screen then the discolouration would have happened sooner, I would have seen the damage when it had happened.

Bearing in mind, I have the report from the inital camera shop I went to, no mention of discolouration or damage to the LCD screen- only that the hinge was loose (See attached). So why is it that after being inspected by this shop- suddenly theres more damage to it? I even showed one of the employees how the screen itself was fine and there was no sort of discolouration- yet one of them kept insisting that this will cause leakage over time, but surely It would have been noticed by a different camera repair shop. Something must have happened during the disassembly, yet they were not honest enough to say anything. And now my camera is in an even worse state because of the LCD screen that was likely damaged by this shop. Please bear in mind as well that it has been nearly a month since I broke this camera so how come the discoloration is only now leaking? very confusing excuses.

So Energy engages in scam-like behaviour; avoid So Energy at all costs.

I transferred to So Energy in September 2025 and have been on the receiving end of a string of errors and appalling customer service from the outset.  Central to all of the problems is So Energy’s gross over estimation of my future gas usage.   In the year to September 2025, I used 18,591kWh of gas.  I am on track to use less than this in my first year with So Energy.  So Energy initially projected my gas usage figure for the year ahead as 68,494kW and, as at April 2026, is still projecting a figure of 48,555kwh per year, which is still more than two and a half times my actual usage rate.

This is not a consequence-free error. So Energy has used its projections to demand grossly inflated monthly direct debits payments, initially at a rate of approaching double what I should be paying (i.e. hundreds of pounds extra per month).  I have been hundreds of pounds in credit with So Energy throughout.  So Energy has never provided any explanation for its projected gas usage figures and when I have pointed out my actual usage figures, So Energy customer services just dismissed these as “not relevant” and stated that it operates in line with “industry norms”.  (I have had it confirmed that the actual Ofgem estimated norm for a property such as mine is 17,000kWh of gas usage per year)  So Energy’s approach just feels like a scam designed to grossly inflate the amount of customer credit it is holding.

I have repeatedly complained to So Energy about matters but it couldn't be bothered to properly review my complaints and said I could take matters to the Energy Ombudsman instead, presumably thinking I wouldn't bother.  Well, I did bother to take matters to the Ombudsman and in its response the Ombudsman, So Energy has apologised for its shockingly poor customer service, offered compensation, promised not to keep trying to increase my monthly payments excessively and conceded that I was entirely right about its grossly over-inflated gas usage projections.

Unbelievably though, even having conceded all points to the Energy Ombudsman, So Energy is still attempting to unjustifiably increase my monthly payments, it still hasn't sorted out the grossly inflated gas projection figure and still hasn’t provided any explanation for how it arrives at its projections.  In addition, someone in So Energy has now apparently decided that the clever thing to do is to just ignore my emails on these recurrent and unresolved issues.  In addition to breaching its own complaint procedures, as well as those of Ofgem, this is really stupid because I am, and always have been, open to an amicable resolution of what are self-evident errors.

*UPDATE 2/4/26: Credit where due; I received two phonecalls. Summary: So Energy -- Awful experience over 7 months. So Energy owe us money and an account correction. Don't recommend.

Our usage data, billing and financial assessment are compromised by TWO fundamental So Energy errors...

ERROR ONE: Compromised meter readings & data.
We began tenancy on a property on 22nd August 2025 (moved in 13/10/25). We were enrolled by a third party without our knowledge, thus we didn't actively choose So Energy as suppliers. Despite being new customers from 22nd August, the previous tenants' meter readings are recorded and associated to our account. They were a family with energy requirements that exceed ours as an older couple without children. This erroneous data is visible and contaminates the assessment of our account and average kWh usage.

Without explanation, So Energy added a new THIRD meter entry to our account on 19th February 2026 and no bills have been issued since. Two billing cycles are overdue. A "Sorry there has been a problem generating your bills, we are working on the problem and will be in touch" error box is displayed throughout the online account, but no one has contacted me. There are now THREE meter entries with associated readings in our account. TWO are compromised by the previous tenants' data history.

ERROR TWO: Incorrect billing.
We're on a SINGLE rate Flex Tariff and our meter only transmits data for the single RATE 1. However, So Energy have also incorrectly charged for a RATE 2 via "estimated" readings since August 2025. We have unwillingly paid additional charges +VAT for a nonexistent, unmetered, unsubscribed RATE 2 (RATE 1 + RATE 2) each billing cycle. Our usage data and charges are compromised by this error.

So Energy -- Poor customer service throughout 7 months of ongoing issues: So Energy appear unwilling to resolve their errors and ignore requests to refund the money owed to us. We raised these issues, with evidence, soon after our account commenced last year. They have also ignored four requests to issue a Deadlock Letter for referral to the Energy Ombudsman.

So Energy -- Poor communication: So Energy have attempted just two phone calls to us in 7 months that couldn't be answered due to work obligations. There is an alternative phone number provided for this reason, which I also emailed within 10 minutes of the first missed call. So Energy have stopped responding to emails. We apparently have a Complaint Manager who rarely responds or provides updates.

So Energy -- Serious financial implications: Our account is always settled and currently in credit despite So Energy's billing errors. However, the Direct Debit requirements are based upon incorrect usage data and have increased substantially. We've been unable to accurately plan our household expenses due to So Energy's continous errors, false charges and incorrect data.

So Energy owe us money and an account correction.

NOTE TO CUSTOMER SERVICE: I politely request that you do not copy & paste a reply here asking us to get in touch. Our complaint number ends in (***)32742. We have been in touch numerous times over 7 months and are consistently ignored.

So the onus is upon you, So Energy, to: Contact us and proactively correct your errors. Refund the money owed to us. Issue accurate bills. Compensate for your errors and inadequacy.

You can update us on action taken via the 2nd phone number provided within our account and over email.

What is even more frustrating is that I was a legitimate customer at the time. I clearly remember providing my vehicle registration in-store, as requested by staff, so I was under the impression that parking was authorised.

The letter I received contained no clear evidence, and when I contacted the parking company to explain the situation, my correspondence was completely ignored.

Following legal advice, I approached the shop manager, who assured me that the issue would be resolved and that I should not worry. Unfortunately, despite this reassurance, three months later I received a court letter stating that I now owe the money.

This situation is extremely stressful and unfair. As a loyal customer, I did not expect to be chased for a parking charge two years later, especially when I followed the process given by the store.

Due to this experience and the lack of proper support or resolution, I will not be shopping at Masala Bazar again.

I strongly advise others to be cautious when using the parking facilities.

I just want to warn others about their car park. There are cameras and a strict 10-minute limit, which isn’t made clear enough. I stayed for around 20 minutes and ended up getting a £170 charge.

I tried to resolve it by speaking to staff, but they told me the manager wasn’t available and refused to help. Later, I found out the case had gone to court without proper communication, and now I’m being asked to pay £270.

This feels very unfair and poorly handled. Be careful if you park there—make sure you’re aware of the time limits, or you could end up in the same situation.

I would like to share my very disappointing experience with Perry Lane Dental Practice.
To begin with, all my dental work prior to coming to Perry Lane had been completed in the UK by qualified specialists, and I have always been covered by a 5-year guarantee on my crown work. I visited this practice hoping for the same level of professionalism, reliability, and care — unfortunately, this was not the case.
I originally chose Perry Lane because of the excellent Google reviews and because I had previously experienced difficult situations with other dentists. I believed a 5-star practice would provide a higher standard of care.
My treatment related to tooth LL6, which needed a crown. Steve quoted me just over £1,000. However, after the crown was fitted, I developed a severe infection that caused nights of unbearable pain. When I returned for help, Steve’s first suggestion was to remove the tooth entirely — which shocked me, as this was immediately after the work he had just completed. I refused, and instead I was given antibiotics. Over time, I ended up with infections four separate times and had to take antibiotics repeatedly.
I repeatedly expressed that the crown felt too high and believed it needed adjusting. Unfortunately, my concerns were ignored, and no one took my suggestions seriously.
I then met with Brittany, the clinical manager. I found her communication abrupt, dismissive, and lacking empathy. As a patient from a different cultural background, I also felt that my concerns were not treated with the same respect or understanding as others. While I cannot speak to anyone’s intentions, the interaction left me feeling judged, talked down to, and culturally misunderstood. This made me extremely uncomfortable. Similar abruptness was also experienced with reception staff on multiple occasions.
The environment at the practice often felt tense, unwelcoming, and unprofessional — more like being told off at school than receiving healthcare.
I had been a patient here for around two years and paid monthly for a plan that included two dental check-ups and two hygienist visits per year. Across those two years, I only received two hygienist appointments instead of four because the practice was consistently fully booked. At one point, my pre-booked hygienist appointment was cancelled because they had no hygienist available.
Both hygienist treatments I did receive were extremely poor. I left with stains still on my teeth — something I’ve never experienced before. When I complained, the hygienist suggested I needed a deep clean “because of the stains,” which made no sense since removing stains is part of a normal hygienist appointment. At the follow-up, a dentist tried scraping stains off manually with a metal tool, without considering potential damage to my enamel. I still left with visible staining.
Overall, I feel the dental plan was not worth the cost, and the service was uncomfortable, dismissive, and far below expected standards. My experience — especially with repeated infections, poor communication, and feeling culturally unheard — has been extremely disappointing.
I cannot recommend this practice based on my experience.
Avoid if possible. 🤯😢😢

I’ve used AnyVan several times in the past for single-item collections and always had a great experience. Unfortunately, our recent 2-bed flat move using their premium service was the complete opposite.

First issue - timing:
AnyVan allows changes up to 24 hours in advance. We rescheduled within this window and received confirmation of the new time. Despite this, the movers arrived at the original (later) time without warning. When we raised this, AnyVan blamed us for changing the booking—even though this was done within their stated policy.

Second issue - incorrect van size:
When the movers arrived, they confirmed that all items were correctly listed on the job sheet, but the van allocated was too small due to an apparent miscalculation on AnyVan's system. When the movers contacted AnyVan, they were reportedly told: “It’s not our problem, you’re the movers.”

Third issue - £1.4k+ premium service not delivered:
We paid for the premium package, which is meant to include packing materials and a full packing service. Due to the delay, we ended up packing most items ourselves to save time - making the upgrade effectively wasted. The materials they brought were also insufficient (around 2 metres of bubble wrap for all fragile items), so we had to use our own linen, towels and even Christmas wrapping paper. There were no proper mattress covers, meaning the mattress was placed directly on the truck floor, and our 65” TV was not boxed - just loosely covered with a blanket.

Fourth issue - incomplete delivery service:
The premium package also includes reassembly and placing items in the correct rooms. However, they arrived so late that everything was simply left in the garage, and nothing was rebuilt.
On top of this, the van couldn’t even stay in place on our slightly inclined driveway - I had to quickly find a rock to stop it rolling, as the brakes were not holding properly.

Having moved before, we specifically paid for a premium, stress-free service - but this ended up being one of the worst moving experiences we’ve had. For comparison, the buyers of our previous flat used Pickfords and had an excellent experience. I would strongly recommend considering them instead.

There seemed to be plenty of staff working, but no one seemed to be very attentive.

one_star_reviews.text:
Poor DSG service & dishonest communication

I took my Audi A4 (B9) here for a DSG service, but the car returned with jerky shifts. The DL382 gearbox in this model is notoriously sensitive to precise oil levels and specific temperatures during the refill process; it is not a "drain and fill" job and requires high technical Diligence.

A few years ago at the Audi dealership, they preformed a dynamic adaption on my gearbox following the service to make sure the shifts are smooth, it's not standard, but it's recommended as I was told.

Because the shifts were messed up, I returned to the garage and asked Steve if he could carry out a dynamic adaptation. Steve confirmed they would do it. When I picked the car up,I asked Steve again wether they have just reset the gearbox to basic settings or done the dynamic adaption, he confirmed that they have done the dynamic adaption, however the odometer showed only 8 miles had been driven. A proper dynamic adaptation for this gearbox requires an extensive, specific drive cycle through all gears 8 miles is physically not enough time to complete it.

I was clearly lied to about the work performed,and when I asked for paperwork, i was given an invoice for £0 that didn't mention any specific work done on the gearbox, just a test drive.

While upshifts slightly improved, the downshifts are still poor and the gearbox is not smooth at all , so I concluded Steve only carried out a reset to basic settings and hasn't done it properly too.

When contacted, Steve refused to acknowledge any wrongdoing and would not cooperate any further.

It is clear that servicing the DL382 is perhaps far beyond this garage’s technical scope. Extremely disappointing services and not to happy about the dishonesty either.

Such a pity that what used to be a decent brand appears to have lost its edge. At least the onion soup was pretty much up to its usual standard.
The same cannot be said for the half roast chicken. The menu promised "Corn-fed chicken from Northern France, slathered in butter, roasted with fresh garlic, rosemary and thyme. Perfect for one." There was no evidence that it was corn fed; perhaps it had been roasted with all those herbs, but their taste had long gone AWOL; if the butter had been slathered at all, there was no sign of it on the plate; the bird had been cooked off in advance and reheated; the pre-cooking was way over - the thing fell apart without having to be "carved"; any French chef worth their salt [sic] would have been mortified by the lack of seasoning; the meat was dry as well as tasteless; it wasn't even half a chicken - the tasty outer 2 sections of the wing had been removed leaving a paltry stump; the fries were pasty and stuck together. I have had great corn fed chicken in Northern France and this was nothing like it. And what is wrong with local chickens? We have wonderful poultry in UK. If the reason for French chicken is for a complete French gastronomic experience, the basics (kindergarten for chefs) need addressing first.
The mussels were OK but the mariniere sauce was bland and under-seasoned.
The final insult was a creme brulee that was runny, lacking the classic taste and texture, covered in some sort of crumb that congealed and did nothing to enhance the dish which was very difficult to eat.
In response to the usual "Is everything all right" I mentioned that it wasn't, but the fact that there was a dissatisfied diner in the building seemed to go unnoticed.
On a positive note, Bristol is well represented with decent eateries so we won't starve.

I booked flights through the company and paid a £400 deposit. An underwhelming kitchen that promised big ideas and outstanding design. I would not recommend this company at all. From start to finish there were many vague aspects, no version control on changes to plans, and  no detail as to how bespoke things would be achieved.

Our kitchen arrived with wine racks that we didn’t order , cheap looking to say the least, and with no plan as to where cupboards were going . Unreal to think it cost 24k and I had no plan drawing .

It was measured wrong and cupboards had to be cut down and doors reordered by the studio as it was their fault. To assist they provided a free labour day to cut the cupboards down and  put it right, but having badly executed it, it made everything worse. Cupboards were not square and every excuse was pointed back to us.

The wrong sinks were delivered and installed , and then we were not able to match the bespoke colour taps with the wastes , as they did not do the wastes in the matching colour as planned, due to a change in sink. We have had to reach a compromise on this which isn’t great. Initially we we were offered two different coloured wastes for the bowl and a half sink which was unbelievable. See pictures. They should have been black with a hint of copper , and yet one was copper and the other brass !!

The island was badly planned and major detail like the extractor had been forgotten. At our cost we had to purchase a worktop mounted extractor as the designer had not factored this in. Another forgotten detail.

Bespoke cupboards arrived flat packed and were put  together wrong by their installer, so new ones had to be ordered. Shelves were not wide enough by 5mm  , and fall down when loaded up, see photos of the brass bracket nearly falling out.

Even now there are bits missing but we’ve had enough. There is also much more to tell . No attention to detail whatsoever. £500 offered for compensation but nothing ever paid.

My overall experience offers advice to avoid this company and go elsewhere, backed up by only 7 positive reviews after 3 and a half years trading??????
